verses.text: In the third year that Belshazzar was king, I, Daniel, had another vision, after the one I had seen before.
In my vision I saw myself in the fortress city of Susa in the province of Elam. In the vision I was beside the Ulai Canal.
I looked up, and there before me was a ram with two horns, standing beside the canal. Both horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.
I watched the ram charge toward the west, the north, and the south. No animal could stand against him, and no one could rescue anyone from his power. He did whatever he wanted and became very great.
As I was thinking about this, suddenly a male goat came from the west, crossing the whole earth so fast that his feet did not touch the ground. The goat had one large horn between his eyes.
He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal, and he charged at him in a furious rage.

I saw him attack the ram in a fury. He struck the ram and broke off both of his horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him. The goat knocked him to the ground and trampled on him, and no one could rescue the ram from his power.
The male goat became very great. But at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off. In its place four large horns grew up, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
Out of one of them came a small horn, which grew very great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the beautiful land of Israel.
It grew until it reached the army of heaven. It threw some of that army and some of the stars down to the earth and trampled on them.
It even set itself up to be as great as the commander of the army of heaven. It took away the daily sacrifice from him, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
Because of rebellion, the army and the daily sacrifice were handed over to it. It threw truth to the ground and succeeded in everything it did.

Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, "How long will the events of this vision last? How long will the daily sacrifice be stopped, and the rebellion that causes ruin go on? How long will the sanctuary and the army of heaven be trampled underfoot?"
He said to me, "It will take two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary will be made right again."
While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there before me stood one who looked like a man.
And I heard a man's voice from the Ulai calling, "Gabriel, explain the vision to this man."
As he came near the place where I was standing, I was terrified and fell face down. He said to me, "Son of man, understand that the vision is about the time of the end."
While he was speaking to me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and raised me to my feet.
He said, "I am going to tell you what will happen later, in the time of God's anger, because the vision is about the appointed time of the end.
The ram with two horns that you saw stands for the kings of Media and Persia.
The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
The four horns that replaced the one that was broken off stand for four kingdoms that will come from his nation, but they will not have his power.
"Near the end of their rule, when the rebels have become completely wicked, a fierce-looking king will rise, a master of trickery.
He will become very strong, but not by his own power. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy powerful people and the holy people.

He will be clever and use deceit to get what he wants. He will think he is great, and he will destroy many who feel safe. He will even rise up against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be destroyed, but not by human power.
"The vision of the evenings and mornings that has been given to you is true. But keep the vision secret, because it is about a time far in the future."
I, Daniel, was worn out and lay sick for several days. Then I got up and went back to the king's business. I was stunned by the vision, and no one could understand it.
